acceptedAnswer.text: A questionnaire maker is a tool that helps you create and share questionnaires online. It lets you add questions, customize the design, and collect responses in one place without technical skills.

Yes. The free plan includes unlimited questionnaires, unlimited responses, all field types, the AI questionnaire generator, drop-off analytics, payment collection, and templates. mainEntity.name: How do I create an online questionnaire?

acceptedAnswer.text: Three ways: pick a template from the questionnaire category, paste a brief and let the AI generator build the structure, or upload a PDF (study protocol, training deck, course outline) for the AI to ground questions in your source. Edit, apply branding, set skip logic, and ship by link, QR, or embed.

mainEntity.name: How does the AI questionnaire generator work?

acceptedAnswer.text: You describe the questionnaire ("post-event satisfaction for a B2B conference, 12 questions, mostly Likert"), upload a PDF for grounding, or paste a list of questions for the AI to format and score. The AI returns a full draft with field types, skip logic, and scoring already wired up. You edit before publishing. Per our DPA, your prompts and uploads are not used to train the AI or to advertise to you.

mainEntity.name: What question types can I use?

acceptedAnswer.text: Single choice, multiple choice, dropdown, rating, Likert scale, matrix, picture choice, short answer, paragraph, file upload, and signature. The AI generator auto-creates single, multiple, dropdown, and true/false out of the box. You add the rest manually after the AI builds the structure.
Question branching shows different questions based on a person’s previous answer. This keeps questionnaires relevant and helps you collect more accurate responses.

mainEntity.name: Can I collect responses if someone doesn’t finish the questionnaire?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Partial submission recovery allows you to capture responses even if a user leaves before completing the questionnaire.

mainEntity.name: How can I share my questionnaire with others?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can share your questionnaire using a direct link, email, QR code, or by embedding it on your website. This makes it easy for anyone to respond from any device.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a questionnaire and a survey?

acceptedAnswer.text: A questionnaire is the instrument: a structured set of written questions designed to collect specific information. A survey is the entire research process that uses the questionnaire, including sampling, distribution, and analysis. A medical history form is a questionnaire; a study using it across 400 patients is a survey. Formester helps you build the questionnaire and run the survey end to end.

mainEntity.name: How long should a questionnaire be?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most use cases, 10-15 questions and under 10 minutes. The Drag'nSurvey study shows completion rates above 80 percent for surveys under 10 minutes vs about 20 percent for long surveys. If you need more depth, split into a screener (under 5 questions) and a follow-up sent only to qualified respondents.

mainEntity.name: Is my respondent data used to train AI or sold to advertisers?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Per the Formester DPA, customer data is not used for analytics, advertising, marketing, or product training. Encryption in transit (TLS) and at rest. Annual third-party penetration testing. Compliant with GDPR,; the security page lists current compliance status.

mainEntity.name: Can I run an academic research questionnaire on Formester?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The free plan supports unlimited responses and includes anonymous submissions, partial submission recovery, all field types, and CSV export for SPSS or R. The AI generator can draft questions from a study protocol PDF.

Instrument quality

Research-grade questionnaires, vetted before respondents see them.

Leading questions, double-barrelled items, absolute phrasing, and prescriptive scales get flagged before the questionnaire goes live. The generator borrows from established questionnaire design (CSAT, NPS, eNPS, pulse) and warns you when an AI-drafted item drifts from those patterns.

Every draft lands in the editor with bias warnings inline. Rewrite the item, change the scale, reorder for response-order effects. Validity is the kind of detail that's hard to retrofit; the editor surfaces it while it's still cheap to fix.

What the editor flags

Five validity checks before launch.

  • Leading items that nudge the respondent toward a specific answer.
  • Double-barrelled items that ask two things at once and produce uncodable responses.
  • Absolute phrasing with 'always,' 'never,' 'every' that force a binary read on a continuous trait.
  • Prescriptive scales where the option labels carry a value judgment ('excellent / poor').
  • Order effects where one item's framing biases the next; reorder warning surfaces in the editor.

Pick the right tool

Questionnaire vs survey vs form. Pick the right tool for the job.

The three terms get used interchangeably. They are not the same thing. The choice changes how you design questions, how you analyze data, and which Formester template you should start from.

Questionnaire Survey Form
What it is The instrument. A structured set of questions. The whole research process: design, sample, distribute, analyze. A data-capture interface for one-off transactions.
Used for Measuring attitudes, opinions, behaviors. Research-grade work. Generalizing findings to a population. Statistical analysis. Booking, signing up, applying, paying, contacting.
Sample size Often small and purposive. Large enough for inference (typically 100+). One respondent per submission.
Question types Likert, rating, ranking, open-ended, multiple choice. Same as questionnaire, plus screeners and quotas. Short answer, dropdown, file upload. Logic optional.
Time to complete 5 to 12 minutes. Same range as the questionnaire it uses. Under 2 minutes is the goal.
Start here Questionnaire templates AI Survey Generator AI Form Generator

A medical history form is a questionnaire. A clinical study using it across 400 patients is a survey. A doctor's appointment booking page is a form. Same input field types, three different jobs.

Benchmarks

What completion rate should you expect?

Knowing the benchmark for your industry tells you whether to push the questionnaire harder or accept the data and ship the analysis.

Use case Typical completion rate What lifts it
Customer feedback (web, email) 20% to 30% Short forms, mobile-first design, branded look
Employee engagement / pulse 30% to 50% Manager endorsement, on-the-clock time, anonymity
Healthcare patient intake 30% to 40% Pre-filling known answers, plain language
B2B SaaS demo or trial form 30% to 38% Logic that hides irrelevant fields
E-commerce post-purchase 28% to 35% Send within 48 hours of purchase
Real estate property inquiry 25% to 35% Mobile-first, three questions or fewer
SMS or WhatsApp questionnaire 40% to 50% Single-question prompts, tap-to-answer

Benchmarks aggregated from third-party industry reports (2026). Cite the original source if you publish results externally.

A questionnaire under 12 questions, optimized for mobile, with skip logic that hides irrelevant fields, generally clears the upper end of the band. Above 30 questions and the rate drops sharply. Industry research shows completion rates above 80% for surveys under 10 minutes vs about 20% for long surveys.

components.markup:
Question types

Question types, and when to use each

Pick the question type that matches the data you actually need. Wrong type, wrong analysis.

Likert scale

Use when measuring intensity of an attitude or opinion. Five-point or seven-point. Keep wording balanced. Don't ask "how strongly do you agree" if you also want neutrals.

Multiple choice

Use for demographic data, factual answers, or pre-defined categories. Easy to analyze, fast to answer. Limit to 5 to 7 options on mobile. Add "Other" only if you'll read open-ended replies.

Open-ended

Use when exploring something you don't know yet, or capturing the language respondents use in their own words. Costs completion rate. Keep to three or fewer per questionnaire.

Ranking

Use when you need a hierarchy of preferences across more than three options. Avoid on mobile (drag-and-drop is finicky). Use forced-choice pairs if respondents are on phones.

Methodology

Built on questionnaire methodology research, not just feature parity

Most form tools sell features. We design the questionnaire builder around the rules that actually move completion rate. Ten to fifteen questions per questionnaire. Under ten minutes to complete. Three or fewer open-ended questions. Mobile-first layouts. Skip logic that hides irrelevant fields instead of asking everyone everything. Pilot-testing before launch.

The product enforces what we can. The dashboard surfaces drop-off pages so you can see where the design fails. The AI generator caps default question counts. Partial Submissions captures the data even when the design loses someone halfway through. The rest is on you, and we will tell you what we know.

Why short matters
"Surveys should be limited to 10 to 15 questions, aiming for a completion time of under 10 minutes. Shorter surveys can achieve completion rates above 80%, whereas longer ones may see rates drop to around 20%."

components.markup:
Privacy and data ownership

Your questionnaire data is yours. We don't train on it.

The brief you write to describe the questionnaire, the AI-generated items, and the responses participants submit are all Customer Data. Per Section 4.4 of our Data Processing Addendum, Formester does not use Customer Data to train AI models, run advertising, run analytics, or feed marketing. The Google Gemini integration that drafts the items inherits the same boundary.

Your account is encrypted at rest, responses move over TLS, and payment data carries an additional AES-256 layer through Stripe. We are GDPR, UK GDPR, and CCPA compliant. We are not SOC 2, ISO 27001, or HIPAA certified yet, and we say so on the security page rather than implying otherwise.

DPA §4.4 · January 2026
"Formester shall not use Customer Data for purposes of analytics, advertising, marketing, or training of artificial intelligence or machine learning models, except as strictly necessary to provide the Services."

Formester Data Processing Addendum, effective January 2026.
